title: Cyrus and the Harbor
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1899, Mirabel Vasquez cuts type in her father's print shop while revolution simmers in the streets. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as conspirators—because her father once promised to print a manifesto for a man now declared enemy of the state—the Vasquez household becomes hunted by both the regime and the rebels who want the manifesto suppressed. Mirabel must honor her father's dying promise to deliver the printed truth before the century turns, navigating betrayal by her brother Tomás, who trades the family's safety for power with the new junta. In the end, Mirabel prints and distributes the manifesto herself from the harbor's last free press, losing the shop but gaining her own name, as the old century dies and an uncertain new one begins.
about_author: Lior Quintana is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring letterpress equipment in coastal archives across the Mediterranean. Their fiction explores how ordinary hands shape history one character at a time.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She works the type cases in her father's print shop while soldiers patrol outside; establish her skill, her invisibility, and the city's unease. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: A Letter Under the Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A sealed letter arrives naming the Vasquez family in a plot to print a seditious manifesto for General Aldana, now declared enemy of the state. Her father burns nothing and says less. Emotional beat: dread arriving on ordinary paper.

chapters.title: What Father Promised
chapters.summary: Father's POV, flashback woven into present. He recalls promising Aldana, in peacetime, that his press would speak when Aldana's voice was silenced. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of an honorable word.

chapters.title: Tomás Ascending
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The elder brother courts the junta's propaganda office, arguing the family can be spared if they inform. Emotional beat: ambition dressing itself up as protection.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She seeks out Aldana's messenger, a smuggler named Reyes, among the harbor's hidden boats. First contact made, trust unearned. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Soldiers in the Shop
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The junta searches the print shop; her father hides the manifesto plates inside a font case of broken type. They pass inspection by inches. Emotional beat: terror compressed into stillness.

chapters.title: The Price Quoted
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The junta offers him his father's shop and a commission in exchange for the plates' location. He asks for three days. Emotional beat: corruption arriving politely, with paperwork.

chapters.title: Broken Type
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She discovers the plates have been found—or moved—and suspects Tomás. Confrontation at the dinner table goes nowhere. Emotional beat: suspicion poisoning the only home she has.

chapters.title: Reyes's Terms
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The smuggler agrees to move Mirabel and the manifesto but demands she print it under her own name, not her father's. Emotional beat: identity offered back like a blade.

chapters.title: The Empty Case
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The plates are gone; Tomás has taken them to trade. Father collapses—his heart, or his shame. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: What the Junta Prints
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. He delivers the plates and watches the junta's printers set lies in his father's typeface. He tells himself it was necessary. Emotional beat: power's first taste turning to ash.

chapters.title: Enemy of Both
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Rebels denounce the Vasquez name for the junta's counterfeit manifesto; the family is now hunted from two directions. Mirabel flees to the harbor. Emotional beat: exile within one's own city.

chapters.title: The Last Free Press
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He reveals a rusted hand-press aboard a condemned hulk in the harbor—the resistance's forgotten relic. Mirabel sees what she must do. Emotional beat: hope found in scrap iron.

chapters.title: Cutting New Type
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With no plates, she begins cutting the manifesto's type by hand, letter by letter, through cold nights. Emotional beat: patience as defiance; craft as conscience.

chapters.title: Tomás's Doubt
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The junta orders him to identify his sister; he realizes they never intended to spare anyone named Vasquez. Emotional beat: the dawning cost of his bargain.

chapters.title: The Raid on the Hulk
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Junta soldiers board the hulk on a tip; Reyes is taken covering her escape with the half-set type. Emotional beat: survival purchased with someone else's freedom.

chapters.title: A Promise Repriced
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, hiding in the salt warehouses. She weighs abandoning the promise against finishing it, remembering her father's hands. Emotional beat: despair interrogated and refused.

chapters.title: Brother at the Door
chapters.summary: Tomás finds her—not to arrest her, but to return the original plates he stole back from the junta's office, buying her hours with his confession. Emotional beat: betrayal answered too late, but answered.

chapters.title: Night Print Run
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On the hulk, she and rebel sympathizers pull the full run of manifestos as dawn approaches and gunboats circle the harbor. Emotional beat: climax—every page pulled against time and tide.

chapters.title: Before the Century Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. On New Year's Eve, the manifesto floods the city—on doorsteps, in fish carts, nailed to the customs house. The crowd reads aloud in the square. Emotional beat: words outpacing guns.

chapters.title: The Cost Tally
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The shop is seized and burned; Tomás is arrested by the men he served; Reyes languishes in custody. Mirabel counts what survival actually cost. Emotional beat: victory with a ledger of losses.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the harbor's edge, she sets her own name in type for the first time and prints a single sheet—a promise kept, a press begun again. Emotional beat: identity claimed; the future opened.
